newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore property firms see slower growth.
newsitem.headline: Singapore property firms see slower growth.

text.p: Singapore property companies fighting an increasingly mature market are expected to report slower earnings growth of around 20 percent for 1996, analysts on Wednesday.

They said the slowdown was expected because of the high base that the companies will be reporting from. Government measures, including a capital gains tax introduced last May to curb property speculation, were also seen as a factor.
"There will be some impact in the 1996 earnings from the curbs. But it is likely to be more of a concern in 1997 and 1998," said Lim Chung Chun, investment analyst with ING Baring Securities.
Lim said he expected the Singapore property sector as a whole to show an 18 percent growth in earnings per share (EPS) for 1996.
This is down sharply from the 32 percent growth in 1995 and from the peak of 39 percent in 1994.
Ng Yeow Tong, investment analyst with GK Goh Securities, said he also expected lower 1996 EPS growth of about 20 percent for local property companies.
He said one of the factors for the lower growth was the slowdown in the residential sector, which has been the main profit generator for property firms.
Taking bluechip City Developments Ltd as an example, he said about 70 percent of the company's profit is from developing and selling homes.
The concensus forecast by analysts polled in the Estimate Directory for CityDev is S$483.6 million (US$340.5 million) for 1996, up from S$400 million in 1995.
The lowest forecast was S$400.2 million while the highest was S$536.8 million.
"I think S$500 million will be the maximum. The company is quite conservative in recognising profits," Ng said.
Another company expected to turn in earnings growth in excess of 20 percent is DBS Land Ltd.
The concensus forecast in the Estimate Directory for DBS Land is net profit of S$212.7 million for 1996, against S$172 million the previous year.
Companies that concentrate on commercial properties, especially in office rentals, are likely to show modest growth.
ING Barings' Lim said these companies, like Singapore Land, depend mainly on rental revisions, and the office rental market had been mostly flat in 1996.
The Estimate Directory concensus forecast for SingLand is a net profit of S$85.4 million for 1996 against S$82.4 million in 1995.
Lim said earnings growth should slow further in 1997 as effects of the government curbs on property speculation flow through.
He said he expected the sector to register 17 percent EPS growth in 1997, with most of the growth accounted for by Marco Polo Development Ltd's phenomenally successful Ardmore Park project.
Marco Polo last year sold 271 units of Ardmore Park apartments, all priced upwards from S$4.5 million each, raking in total sales of about S$1.5 billion.
"But excluding Marco Polo, the sector is expected to show earnings growth of seven percent," Lim said.
